- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.7), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in the 10–15 day horizon; if sentiment is mixed or neutral, add a small upward bias to account for lingering momentum.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-cycle peaks; if sentiment turns bullish late in the window, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to capture tail-end momentum.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in the last 5–7 days to reflect sentiment shift.
